description: The Ecosystem Services Valuation Database is described by its makers as the largest publicly available database of standardised monetary values for ecosystem services, covering all ecosystem services and all biomes on all continents with global coverage. It holds 12,905 values standardised to international dollars of 2020 per hectare per year, drawn from a repository of 2,841 studies, of which 1,541 are included, taken from over 30 years of peer-reviewed research and official reports; 68 percent of values are externally reviewed. It is developed by Brander Economics and the Foundation for Sustainable Development with partners including FAO, IUCN and the European Commission, and a 2026 data update has been released. The database is accessible online through a web application at esvd.net after free registration, with more than 10,400 registered users, and content is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. Caveats: values are transferred from primary studies of varying method and context, so benefit transfer to a new site carries large uncertainty, and the web application needs JavaScript and an account. It supports economic appraisal of green and blue infrastructure and nature-based solutions for climate adaptation, for example valuing flood regulation or cooling services in cost-benefit analysis; related records are Oppla and CLIMADA.
